subject: Sales discovery: model fit & benchmarks — FinTechCo (next steps)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Samuel Kim <samuel.kim@fintechco.com>
Cc: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-16T17:00:00-07:00
Subject: Sales discovery: model fit & benchmarks — FinTechCo (post-call recap)

Thanks for the time today, Sam — helpful conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our end: 

Summary of needs:
- Real-time chat for customer support: multi-turn, slot-filling, and knowledge retrieval.
- Throughput target: ~150 TPS peak for 2k concurrent users (burst to 250 TPS).
- Latency SLO: p95 < 250ms for short responses (<300 tokens).
- Data residency: US-only, and SOC2 / audit logs required.

Initial model fit recommendations:
- Redwood-13B-v2 (quantized) — best cost/latency balance for chat and retrieval-augmented prompts.
- Llama2-70B-instruct (quantized int8) — stronger long-form and creative completions; higher cost.
- Option: ensemble fallback to smaller model for short answers to preserve latency.

Proposed evaluation plan:
1) You share a representative prompt set / sample logs (we discussed permissioned subset). I attached the prompt_set_v1.jsonl we discussed as a template.
2) We'll run a 48-hour benchmark on our Dedicated infra (US region) using your sample workload.
3) We'll share a Redwood-verified performance profile (TPS, p50/p90/p95 latencies, token cost) + prompts-level quality metrics and sample outputs.

Immediate asks for you:
- Confirm ok to run benchmarks on the sample prompts attached (and provide any additional do-not-include examples).
- Point us to a procurement contact (cc'd welcome) for next steps if you want an official quote.

Attachments: prompt_set_v1.jsonl (template)

Happy to jump on a quick follow-up next week to review profiles. Proposed slots: Tue/Wed morning PST.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachment stub: prompt_set_v1.jsonl (JSONL, 12KB)

From: Samuel Kim <samuel.kim@fintechco.com>

Date: 2026-07-16T20:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sales discovery: model fit & benchmarks — FinTechCo (post-call recap)

Thanks, Marissa — that recap matches our notes. A few clarifications before we give the go-ahead:

1) When you say "Redwood-verified performance profile", can you share an example of the metrics you publish? I want to make sure we can interpret TPS vs latency tradeoffs correctly.
2) Does your Dedicated infra support preemptible bursts for spikes? We need to know how autoscaling/burst would affect p95.
3) Privacy: we will only share de-identified prompts. Do you require an NDA for running a benchmark on our sample prompts?

Also cc'ing procurement (procurement@fintechco.com) so they have visibility. If the benchmark shows good fit, procurement will need an expected TCO and any required lead times for dedicated capacity.

—Sam

FinTechCo

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Samuel Kim <samuel.kim@fintechco.com>
Cc: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-17T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sales discovery: model fit & benchmarks — FinTechCo (benchmarks & profiles)

Great questions — answered inline below and sharing links to an example profile + our benchmark dashboard.

1) Example Redwood-verified performance profile: we publish per-model profiles that include:
   - Peak sustained TPS (for specific sequence length mixes), p50/p90/p95 latencies (ms), memory footprint, and recommended batch/kv cache configs.
   - Cost estimate per 1M tokens for the measured config.
   - Known regressions or quality tradeoffs when using specific quantization settings.

For reference, here are quick summary numbers from a recent dedicated-run (Redwood-13B-v2, quantized int8; sequence mix: 75% short prompts <128 tokens / 25% long):
   - Sustained TPS: 220 TPS (US-dedicated-8g pool)
   - p50 latency: 38 ms
   - p90 latency: 120 ms
   - p95 latency: 210 ms
   - Avg tokens/sec per GPU: ~1450 tokens/sec

Notes: the numbers above are for our default batching + KV cache settings. Short-turn conversations with aggressive KV caching typically improve p50 by ~10–20ms.

2) Autoscaling & burst: yes — Dedicated supports controlled burst capacity. We can configure a burst policy (e.g., +30–40% for 10–30 minute windows) with an autoscale cooldown. Burst will increase p95 during the scale-up window; we instrument that and include a "burst-adjusted p95" in the profile we share.

3) Privacy & NDA: for benchmarking de-identified prompts we do not require an NDA. If you want us to accept raw logs with identifiers, we require a data processing addendum.

Attached: redwood_verified_profiles.pdf (example profile) and link to the interactive dashboard: https://redwood-inference.app/benchmarks/fintechco-2026. The Drive folder has raw CSVs and per-prompt quality buckets: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2B3C-fintechco-benchmarks

Quality/regression note: we include a prompt-set level "quality delta" metric comparing base model -> quantized variant. If you have a small number of safety/financial-compliance prompts, we flag those and run extra evals to surface regressions.

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm permission to run benchmark on the de-identified prompt_set_v1 (no NDA needed).
- We run the 48-hour dedicated benchmark and share the Redwood-verified profile + per-prompt quality report.
- Optional: schedule a 30-min review with Alex (technical solutions) and Dylan (benchmark ops) to walk results and discuss rollout.

If that sounds good I can kick off the run as early as tomorrow afternoon.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_verified_profiles.pdf (PDF, 420KB); Dashboard link: https://redwood-inference.app/benchmarks/fintechco-2026
